metadata.title: डायन कौन होती है | आदिवासियों में डायन प्रथा | Witch Hunting Case Study | Ground Report
metadata.description:
Witch-hunting remains one of the gravest and most deep-rooted crimes affecting Adivasi communities in India. The practice, fuelled by superstition, social tensions, and systemic neglect, continues to claim innocent lives—most brutally women. Among the worst-affected regions is Mayurbhanj district in Odisha, where recurring cases make it one of the most dangerous hotspots for this crime. Jharkhand too has been grappling with the same menace, with victims often targeted under the guise of “dayan” or “witch” branding.
In this hard-hitting investigation, Chitrita Sanyal of Main Bhi Bharat travels deep into these vulnerable communities to uncover the human stories behind the statistics. Her report brings to light the fear, stigma, and violence that survivors face, and exposes the social and structural failures that allow witch-hunting to persist even today. Through conversations with families of victims, tribal leaders, women’s groups, and rights activists, the investigation asks a crucial question: why does such a brutal practice continue, and what will it take to end it?
This powerful story is not just about crime—it is about justice, dignity, and the urgent need for protection of tribal women’s rights.
